item.title: Version 1.0.0-beta.25
item.description:
1.0.0-beta.25

Teach Scribio from anywhere it writes, an industry glossary for your field, a cleaner AI settings page, and a Scribio that stays in the Dock and keeps its memory in check.

Teach Scribio

  • Teach from any line Scribio wrote. Point at a summary line, decision, next step, task, moment, title or AI answer and choose ✦ Teach. Say what's wrong in your own words — a spelling, a person, "this was decided" — and Scribio shows exactly what it will change. Nothing changes until you press Apply, and every change can be undone.
  • Teach from the transcript. Select a word such as "click" and tell Scribio it should be "Qlik". The first answer appears instantly; Scribio's AI adds to it in the background.
  • A teach bar on the Summary takes several corrections at once.
  • Taught words reach everything Scribio writes — summaries, the meeting record, titles, moments and Scribio AI — and past summaries that used the old spelling update in the background. An ordinary word (like "click" the verb) is left alone where it's meant.

Glossary

  • A new Glossary page in Settings for names, products and acronyms, with search, filters, how often each term appears, and import and export.
  • Acronyms are spelled out the first time in a summary, for example "Project Management Office (PMO)".
  • Industry glossaries for Technology & Communications, Financial Services, Insurance, Health Care, US Public Sector and Logistics, reviewed term by term. They're off until you turn one on; Scribio suggests one when your meetings use its terms. Your own terms always win, and you can hide any term.
  • Terms defined out loud are learned. When you say "ARR, which is our annual recurring revenue", Scribio remembers it. Definitions from other people apply to that meeting first and everywhere once someone else confirms them.
  • A wrong meaning is easy to fix: select the term in the transcript and choose Not here, Never this meaning, or It means….

AI settings

  • A calmer AI page: your model in plain words, a writing style, and a few facts about you and your work. Technical transcription controls moved to Diagnostics.
  • "Spellings to confirm" is gone, and so is the background scan behind it.

Meetings and people

  • Select several meetings by hovering a row and ticking it, then add them to a project, tag them, refresh their details or delete them.
  • Tags you choose on any meeting, alongside the automatic ones.
  • The People pane shows who spoke how much, with a card for each person: what they owe you and what they talked about.
  • A speaker card opens beside a speaker's name with a larger picture, their details, See more and Teach.
  • Search lands on the word you searched, highlighted in the transcript; ⌘G and ⇧⌘G step through the matches.

Windows and the menu bar

  • Scribio stays in the Dock. Yellow minimizes like any Mac app; red quits.
  • Only the small recording pill floats above other apps, including full-screen meetings. Hover it to minimize it to the Dock.
  • The menu bar icon follows your menu bar's colours, with a blue dot while recording and no text.
  • "Scribio" is capitalised everywhere you see it.

Recording and summaries

  • Back-to-back calls are split into separate meetings when a new call is confirmed.
  • Chat apps sitting idle no longer start a countdown.
  • Playback on speakers no longer echoes the other side of the call.
  • Microphone restarts are steadier when devices change.
  • Names you settle reach the summary, tasks and moments, and old "Unknown voice" labels are rewritten.

Also

  • Memory stays in check. Scribio keeps one copy of its AI model, unloads it when idle, and waits with automatic AI work when your Mac is short on memory.

item.title: Version 1.0.0-beta.24
item.description:
1.0.0-beta.24

Chatting in Teams no longer starts a recording, every screen updates as soon as something changes, and meetings take their calendar title.

Recording

  • Chatting in Teams no longer starts a recording. Moving between Teams chats could look like joining a meeting, because Teams gives chats and meetings the same kind of window title. Scribio now waits for a sign of a real call — Teams using the microphone, playing call audio, or reporting a call in progress — and starts within seconds of joining. The minutes you spend waiting in a Teams lobby before the call starts are no longer recorded.
  • A notification sound is not a call. A single chime from a chat app no longer counts as a call starting.
  • Meetings cut off by a crash or a forced quit keep their real length. Their end time now comes from the audio itself, and meetings that earlier showed as hours long are corrected automatically.

Everything stays up to date

  • Every screen updates as soon as something changes. Rename or merge a speaker, move a line, tick off a task, or let a background update finish, and the meeting list, Summary, Actions, Intelligence, Tasks, search and People pages all show the change without opening the meeting again. A note or task you are typing is never overwritten.
  • During a recording, screens you are not looking at refresh at a slower pace, so the recording is never slowed down.

Meeting titles

  • A meeting takes its calendar event's name. When Scribio is sure which event a meeting belongs to, the meeting is named after it; otherwise it keeps the name Scribio writes. A name you typed always wins.
  • Calendar names are cleaned up: prefixes such as RE:, FW:, FWD:, [EXTERNAL] and Updated invitation: are removed, including stacked ones and common versions in other languages.
  • Past meetings are renamed too, a few at a time in the background. If your work calendar is not available on this Mac (for example the account was removed from the Calendar app), Scribio waits for it rather than giving up.

Also

  • Background work is safer when more than one copy of Scribio is open, and anything it had to postpone runs as soon as it can.

item.title: Version 1.0.0-beta.23
item.description:
1.0.0-beta.23

Calls on Bluetooth earbuds are transcribed in full again, the speech an earlier beta lost is recovered by itself, and the live view, speaker naming and summaries have all been reworked.

Calls and recording

  • The other side of a call is no longer dropped on Bluetooth earbuds. With earbuds in call mode, most of what the other people said could go missing from the transcript. That is fixed, and Scribio now checks during every meeting that the call is reaching the transcript.
  • Speech that was lost is recovered by itself. Scribio now saves the call as its own file beside your microphone. For meetings where the other side's speech went missing, Scribio transcribes it again from that file in the background — a few meetings per launch, never during a recording — and rebuilds the summary. On a call with just one other person, the recovered lines are given that person's name.
  • No more phantom recordings from Teams. A Teams survey or chat window left open after a call, or a Teams window already open when Scribio starts, no longer starts a recording on its own. A real call is still picked up as soon as it starts.
  • Stop means stop. After you press Stop, Scribio waits for the meeting to really end before it offers to record that meeting again. A meeting in one app ending no longer stops a recording in another, and back-to-back meetings across apps are offered.
  • Earbuds in call mode record, and the "can't hear your microphone" warning no longer appears when the call is coming through.
  • The microphone follows your Mac's current input mid-meeting, and switching headsets no longer ends the meeting.

The live view

  • A small bar is the default during a recording. Expand it to a compact view with the transcript, people, notes and Ask; Expand again opens the main window's Meetings page, and "Back to live view" in the sidebar returns you to it.
  • The live windows are normal windows. They no longer float over everything; click Scribio in the Dock to bring them back.
  • A new menu bar icon that follows your menu bar's colours.
  • Notes: the note bar can be moved and resized, Screenshot picks a window or a region you drag (double-click for the whole screen), and the AI reads a screenshot's most useful text.

Speaker names

  • Name a voice once, and it carries over. One panel names every voice in a meeting, with a clip to listen to; a name you give reaches the same voice in other meetings on a strong match. Every change can be undone.
  • Move a single line to the right person; a line you set by hand is never changed automatically.
  • Unknown voices keep one number across meetings, and a guessed name is shown as a suggestion, never as a name.
  • Names match everywhere — the transcript, the People pane and the live view use the same name, and the People pane updates as soon as you rename someone.
  • Action items belong to the person who said them, and your own voice is no longer learned under someone else's name. Past meetings are corrected automatically.
  • A whole room on one microphone is split into its voices first; if it cannot be split, those lines are left unnamed rather than given to you.
  • Faces: the People pane shows a speaker's face where Scribio has one, and face crops are sharper. Face recognition is asked for once, never during a call, and turning it on in Settings counts as your consent.
  • The speaker picker is wider, picks the top match with Return, and lists the people you named most recently.

Summaries

  • You can see what the summary is doing — "Reading topic 4 of 9", "Writing the summary" — instead of a bar that looks stuck, and it finishes faster.
  • Summaries read your pinned notes and screenshots, and quotes credit the right speaker.

Also

  • Click a transcript line to play it. Playback now includes both sides of the call.
  • The graph opens fitted, zooms and pans, and has a small map that jumps where you click.
  • Text size in Settings scales every font.
  • Backups are kept compressed, with one weekly backup kept for 60 days.
  • An update can no longer corrupt or strand your library, and an interrupted model download resumes cleanly.
  • Topics is gone from the sidebar (it was the same as Graph), and the "All systems healthy" line is gone from the bottom of the window.

item.title: Version 1.0.0-beta.22
item.description:
1.0.0-beta.22

Meetings with too many speakers are actually cleaned up now, and Settings shows the cleanup while it runs.

Speaker identification

  • Meetings with too many speakers are cleaned up for real. beta.21's cleanup re-ran speaker identification on these meetings but left most of their "Speaker N" rows in place. Scribio now listens to each such meeting again, works out how many voices it really holds, and joins the "Speaker N" rows that are the same voice. A row that is the same voice as a named person becomes that person. A row that mixes two voices is split up line by line. Every meeting that beta.21 already went through is cleaned up once more, in the background, newest first and never during a recording.
  • What is never changed: names you typed or confirmed yourself, names from your calendar, and your own name. When one voice could belong to either of two named people, Scribio leaves it alone rather than guess. Lines from your microphone and lines from the call are never joined.
  • Every join can be undone in Settings → Diagnostics → Recent Merges. Lines moved one by one are recorded but cannot be undone from there; you can still move any line to the right person yourself.

Settings

  • Upgrade Past Meetings shows a background upgrade while it runs, with how many meetings it has done, and greys out the Run buttons until it finishes. Before, a background upgrade showed nothing, and pressing Run started a second copy of the same work.
  • The past-meeting settings describe what runs on its own. "Ask me" and "Automatic" now say that meetings left with too many speakers are fixed without asking. Choosing Manual still turns this off.

Also new if you're coming from beta.20

If you skipped beta.21, this update brings its fixes too:

  • Closing the lid after a meeting no longer breaks its processing. The work pauses while the Mac sleeps and carries on when it wakes.
  • Reprocess works again, and a summary that runs out of room in Apple Intelligence is trimmed until it fits.
  • The summary model downloads by itself on Macs with 16 GB of memory or more, once setup is done and never during a recording. A model already on your Mac is never downloaded again, and a download that stops partway resumes where it stopped.
  • The window stays where you can reach it, even when it was taller than the screen or slipped under the Dock.
  • Speakers come out named more often: names on Teams and Zoom tiles are read more reliably, including the highlighted border around whoever is speaking.
  • Fuller summaries for earlier meetings: click Upgrade Now when Scribio offers to upgrade past meetings, or Regenerate on a meeting's Summary tab.

item.title: Version 1.0.0-beta.21
item.description:
1.0.0-beta.21

Meetings finish after the lid closes, Reprocess works again, and speakers come out named.

Fixed

  • Closing the lid after a meeting no longer breaks its processing. The work pauses while the Mac sleeps and carries on when it wakes, instead of timing out. While a meeting is being finished, the Mac waits before going to sleep on its own; closing the lid still puts it to sleep.
  • Reprocess works again. When an Apple Intelligence summary ran out of room, Scribio fell back to a summary model that was not on the Mac, so the summary failed. Apple Intelligence now trims the transcript until the summary fits, and Scribio falls back only to a model it actually has.
  • The summary model downloads by itself, and is used. After this update, a Mac with 16 GB of memory or more downloads the summary model in the background from Scribio's server, once setup is done and never during a recording. If setup never finished and you had not chosen a model, that model becomes your summary model, as a finished setup would have made it. A model you chose yourself, Apple Intelligence included, is kept.
  • Fuller summaries for earlier meetings. Once the summary model is on your Mac, new meetings use it. For meetings recorded before, click Upgrade Now when Scribio offers to upgrade past meetings, or open a meeting's Summary tab and click Regenerate. A summary you wrote or edited yourself is never replaced.
  • Model downloads resume. If a summary or speech model download stops partway, the next try carries on where it stopped instead of starting over. A model already on your Mac is never downloaded again.
  • A clearer message when a model is missing. It no longer blames security software.
  • The window stays where you can reach it. If it is taller than your screen or its bottom edge slips under the Dock, Scribio pulls it back so you can resize it again. This also happens after you unplug a larger display.
  • Opening Scribio from the menu bar or the live meeting window no longer resizes the wrong window.

Speaker identification

  • Fewer phantom speakers. After a meeting, Scribio no longer creates extra speakers from fragments of someone's speech; those lines go to the right person.
  • Earlier meetings with too many speakers are cleaned up automatically. After this update, Scribio re-identifies the speakers of any past meeting that has more speakers than it could have had, in the background, newest first and never during a recording. Names you typed in yourself are kept. Choosing Manual for past-meeting upgrades in Settings turns this off.
  • Names on Microsoft Teams tiles are read. This includes names shown only briefly while you resize the window. An invitee's name counts after one sighting.
  • Scribio sees who is speaking on Teams and Zoom. It reads the highlighted border the app draws around the speaker's tile, including Zoom's thin green one, so names land on the right voices.
  • More names are read on large galleries. Scribio reads the meeting window in sections, so small name labels on a big Zoom gallery or speaker strip are no longer missed. An invitee's name is read even when their face isn't visible.
  • Tile names are read correctly. Scribio re-reads each name label up close, which fixes one-letter misreadings, and ignores the signal-strength icon next to your own name.
  • You are marked in your own invite lists, so you are not counted as one of the other participants.
  • Slack huddles: a 1:1 huddle is still named from its title. Scribio now also measures what a huddle window shares with macOS, so multi-person huddles can be named in a later update.

Setup and models

  • Guided setup asks for all five permissions, where backups go, and which calendar accounts to read. Nothing records by itself until setup is finished.
  • Move to Applications is offered on first launch.
  • The speech model downloads from Scribio's server during setup, with one progress bar for both models. An older or missing speech or summary model is replaced in the background after an update.
  • A 5-second countdown before the microphone opens when you record your voice sample.

item.title: Version 1.0.0-beta.20
item.description:
1.0.0-beta.20

Scribio's new look, a structured record of every meeting, and meetings joined in a browser.

Before you update

  • Scribio now requires macOS 26 (Tahoe) or later. On Macs with less memory, Apple Intelligence writes the summaries, and macOS 26 is the first release where an app can use it. Macs on macOS 15 keep the version they have and are no longer offered updates.

New look

  • The Evil Genius design. A new palette, typeface and app icon (seven bars on navy), with Start recording as the one orange button on screen.
  • A guided setup with a brand rail. Permissions on cards, a recommended summary model that downloads while setup carries on, and calendar, backups, updates, summary style and voice in one pass.
  • Settings reorganised. About, Integrations, Storage › Backup & restore, and Diagnostics as Support and Maintenance.

Meetings

  • A structured record of each meeting. Topics, decisions, proposals, actions, risks and open questions, each with the quoted lines it came from.
  • A redesigned Summary tab. One column of rows, a timeline strip that is also the player, a collapsible inspector, and a summary written for the reader you choose.
  • Every jump into the transcript lands on its line and stays marked.
  • Titles. A meeting takes its calendar subject when the match is certain, and you can rename any meeting.
  • Tasks, Graph and Intelligence pages redesigned. A task list with a board by status and projects on tasks; the Graph with Focus and Connections; Intelligence as a briefing.

Recording

  • Meetings joined in a browser are detected and recorded. This covers Zoom, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams and other services in Safari, Chrome, Edge, Firefox and other browsers.
  • The live meeting screen is redesigned. It has a roomier note box, screenshots at the moment, Mark next step / Mark decision, and sentiment while you record.
  • Ask Scribio AI during a recording with the model you chose.
  • Saving a meeting's audio can be switched off in the middle of a meeting.
  • Window buttons. Yellow hides Scribio from the Dock and keeps it in the menu bar; red quits. During a recording Scribio asks first, then stops and saves before quitting.

Speaker identification

  • Microsoft Teams calls: Scribio now listens to the Teams process that plays the call. It used to hear silence there, so it could not tell you from the other side and left extra unnamed speakers. Earlier Teams meetings cannot be repaired automatically; merge their placeholder speakers by hand.

Models

  • Below 16 GB of memory, Apple Intelligence is the default summariser. From 16 GB, Qwen3.5 9B is the default.
  • Models download from Scribio's own server first, with a progress bar. They follow your Mac's proxy settings, and Hugging Face is the fallback.

Fixed

  • Long meetings get a complete record instead of stopping partway.
  • A link inside a summary asks before it opens.
  • NDA clean only puts a cleaned copy on your clipboard after it passes every check.

item.title: Version 1.0.0-beta.19
item.description:
1.0.0-beta.19

Fixes beta.18, which would not open on macOS 26 or earlier — macOS reported that Scribio "cannot be opened because of a problem". Everything new in beta.18 is included.

Fixed

  • Scribio opens again on macOS 26 (Tahoe). beta.18 was built in a way that required macOS 27 without saying so.

item.title: Version 1.0.0-beta.18
item.description:
1.0.0-beta.18

Mostly stability and speaker naming. If you are on beta.16 or beta.17, Check for Updates will find this one.

New

  • Long meetings are summarised end to end. Scribio now reads a long meeting in parts and combines them, so what was said in the middle of a call makes it into the summary.
  • The summary arrives sooner. Chapters and search indexing now run after it instead of before it.
  • iCloud Drive and OneDrive can be chosen as backup locations. iCloud Drive backups appear in Finder in the Scribio Backups folder in iCloud Drive.
  • A speaker still shown as "Speaker N" now says why no name was found and offers the fix.
  • Asking the chat about all meetings now searches your transcripts and summaries by what you typed, and says so when nothing matches instead of answering from unrelated passages.

Fixed

  • Scribio could freeze for minutes during or after a call — in the Live Meeting Companion's transcript and in AI Chat. Both are fixed, and if the window ever freezes anyway, Scribio now restarts itself rather than staying stuck.
  • Minimizing the Live Meeting Companion quit Scribio. Opening Settings → iCloud could also quit it.
  • Deleting a meeting now deletes its recording. Recordings left behind by meetings deleted earlier can be removed with Review Reclaimable Space, in the Field Capture section of Settings → Diagnostics.
  • After moving your library to a new Mac, older meetings play again.
  • A meeting where you are the only one speaking is named as you — and Scribio now checks the voice is actually yours first, so a video playing into your microphone is no longer credited to you.
  • The Updates status no longer reads "checked in 48m" for a check that already happened.

item.title: Version 1.0.0-beta.17
item.description:
1.0.0-beta.17

The first Scribio release delivered as an update rather than a download. If you are on beta.16, Check for Updates should find this one.

New

  • Setup now ends by telling you what it already found — permissions, your calendar, backups, and your voice with the date you enrolled it. Steps that were already done used to be dropped silently, which made a finished setup look like a skipped one.
  • Settings → About → Updates: install automatically, hold an update while a recording is running, and a line saying when Scribio last looked.
  • Check for Updates… is now in the Scribio menu and the menu bar, and About shows a Beta channel badge while beta updates are on.

Fixed

  • Your voice: "enrolled" now means a voiceprint this Mac can actually use. A profile carried over from another Mac — whose encryption key stayed behind by design — used to satisfy setup while recognising nobody. If enrolment is missing or was skipped, Scribio now says so instead of waiting for a meeting.
  • Microsoft 365 asks for your calendar only. Meeting attendance reports are requested later, if you turn them on — so the first approval your organisation sees is the smallest one that works.

item.title: Version 1.0.0-beta.16
item.description:
1.0.0-beta.16

Fixed

  • Setup → Calendar: one Allow now flips the row. The OS's answer is trusted instead of a status read that lagged it.
  • Microsoft 365: a refusal is worded honestly (cancelled, or your organisation must approve Scribio once) and the IT approval link is offered from setup.
  • Updates: this is the first build that can receive updates. Every earlier build shipped without its update configuration, so install this one from the DMG — the next release arrives through Check for Updates.

New

  • Setup asks once how Scribio updates itself: automatic checks (on) and beta updates (off).
